claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr is a single-phase BCC solid solution.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has high strength at room temperature.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr retains high strength around 1000 °C.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of approximately 10.21 g/cm³.
Approximately 10 at% Hf should be replaced with Al while leaving the other elemental fractions unchanged.
The Al-substituted HfMoTaTiZr alloy will remain a single-phase BCC solid solution.
Al-induced lattice distortion will retain solid-solution strengthening.
Replacing heavy Hf with lighter Al will reduce the alloy's average atomic mass and density.
Preservation of a homogeneous BCC solid solution will keep strength and high-temperature stability intact.
Low-density Al has been used in other high-entropy alloys to tailor mechanical and thermal performance.
A Ti-V-Zr-Nb alloy containing 10 at% Al formed a single-phase BCC solid solution in the as-cast state.
The proposed alloy will have at least 5–10% lower density than as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
The proposed alloy will maintain or only slightly change yield strength and ductility at room temperature.
The proposed alloy will maintain or only slightly change yield strength and ductility around 1000 °C.
The proposed applicability range is room temperature through approximately 1000 °C under tensile and compressive loading.
The hypothesis is rejected if density decreases by less than 5%, or if yield strength or ductility decreases by more than 10% at either room temperature or approximately 1000 °C.

contradictions.description: Replacing only approximately 10 at% Hf implies that residual Hf remains, nominally giving Hf10Al10Mo20Ta20Ti20Zr20 if 10 percentage points are replaced. In contrast, the labels AlMoTaTiZr used in the intervention and experiment omit Hf and conventionally suggest complete Hf replacement.

The hypothesis says mechanical properties will be preserved or kept intact, whereas the rejection rule accepts reductions in yield strength or ductility of up to 10%, which constitutes a measurable sacrifice.
